failure_modes: Assay insensitivity or capture-reagent incompatibility yields false negatives in low-biomass lavage/CSF samples, preventing detection of capture-positive, particle-co-localized fractions (false failure).

Species- or formulation-dependent delivery barriers (scale-up from rodent to target species or even assay-aliquot handling) result in genuine absence of intact EVs in sampled compartments, so the bridge cannot be demonstrated despite EV activity in the source material (true negative for the hypothesis).

Soluble secretome or non-vesicular particles present in captured/eluted fractions mediate ex vivo cytokine modulation, so membrane-disruption or capture-depletion controls fail to cleanly distinguish EV-associated activity (confounding positive readout).
Labeling/spike-in tracers or fractionation steps alter EV stability or bioactivity, producing artifactual loss or gain of ex vivo effect and misleading conclusions about intact-EV necessity.

Short post-dose sampling misses relevant kinetics (either too early or too late) and produces irreproducible linkage between in vivo verification and ex vivo readout, making the attribute unmeasurable/reliably reproducible.
Particle-count-matched capture-depletion may be technically infeasible or incompletely achieved, so comparator arms are not truly matched and results become uninterpretable.

Inter-animal and inter-lot variability exceed effect size (low signal-to-noise), so multiple replicates still fail to meet qualitative reproducibility criteria and the potency gate cannot be validated.
strongest_objection: The single strongest, bounded reason this proposal could fail is that intranasal intact-EV exposure after dosing is biologically and/or practically undetectable in the sampled proximal compartments (nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa) despite correct assay design, so the orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridge cannot be established. A negative bridge could reflect true delivery failure in the chosen species/route (not assay artifact) and therefore preclude demonstrating any intact-EV–linked potency even if rodent efficacy signals exist.
